hook_text: This skull has fangs, it is older than the dinosaurs, and it is made of solid stone. How?
clip_script: Nieu-Bethesda, in the Karoo. About 255 million years ago, an animal dies by a river. A flood buries it in mud. The skin and muscles rot away. Layers pile up and harden into rock. Water carries minerals that slowly turn the bones to stone. Millions of years later, erosion wears the rock away, and there it is. A fossil! A page from the history of life.
visual_style: Whiteboard timeline: animal by a river, mud covering it, layers piling up, bones turning grey, then a fossil hunter with a brush.
pacing: Slow, step-by-step story, then a big reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look closely at the rocks next time you are in the Karoo.
